subject: Spend compression & ops constraints — post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@crescentpay.com>, Maya Lopez <maya.lopez@crescentpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Spend compression & ops constraints — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Alex / Maya —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment before I follow up with a compact pilot quote. I kept this focused on the cost levers we discussed (batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization) and the operational constraints you flagged.

What we heard (pain & constraints)
- Peak wallet verification latency needs: 95th percentile < 220ms for auth flows (mobile).
- Strict monthly budget cap: internal cap ~$18k/mo for inference during trial (you mentioned procurement gating at $20k).
- Predictable unit economics over variable traffic (seasonal spikes tied to promos).
- Data residency: US-only; logs for evals can be shared to a limited S3 bucket.

Goals you stated
- Validate a production-like pilot that keeps unit cost within the budget envelope while preserving latency targets.
- Get a first-month sample cost to present to procurement and engineering by next Wed (6/4).
- See dashboard-level observability (per-route latency + token burn) during pilot.

Quick nucleus of the cost approach (assumptions for our sample model)
- Token profile (avg per request): 160 input tokens, 180 output tokens (320 total).
- Baseline model variant: open-llm-2-13b (float32) equivalent performance; we’ll present quantized variants for savings.
- Batching: conservative batching for auth flows (batch window 8–15ms) — expect 12–20% token cost reduction for your mix.
- Prefix/KV caching: goal is to cache repeated prompt prefixes for templates (estimated hit rate: 12–18%) — additional 8–12% cost reduction.

Sample monthly math (illustrative)
- Estimated monthly requests in trial: 120k requests
- Avg tokens/request: 320 -> ~38.4M tokens/month
- Baseline hosted cost (no batching/caching): ~$1,150 - $1,600 (per million tokens range dependent on model variant) -> ballpark $44k - $61k/month
- With batching + cache + 4-bit quantization candidate -> projected reduction 55–70% -> estimated $13k - $27k/month

Bottom line: with conservative batching and prefix caching plus a quantized inference path, we can plausibly bring CrescentPay into procurement’s ~$18k/month envelope for the trial while keeping 95p latency near your 220ms target. We’ll validate exact numbers once we see a 30-day token profile.

Requests / next steps
1) Can you share a 30-day token-level sample (anonymized) or grant read access to a temporary S3 bucket so we can run the spend model against your actual distribution? File format CSV is fine — sample column names in the attached spreadsheet.
2) Confirm decision timeline for procurement (you mentioned 6/10 latest?) so we align pilot dates.
3) If you want, we can run two quick micro-profiles: quantized variant + baseline float variant and return per-token cost + latency SLOs within 48 hours of receiving the sample.

Attachments: redwood_spend_model_v1.xlsx (simple calculator), crescentpay_token_profile_sample.csv (expected schema)

I’ll prepare a compact pilot quote and a 4-week scope doc once we have the sample. If that works, I’ll propose a 30-min kickoff next Tue (6/2) or Wed (6/3).

Thanks again —

Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182


From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@crescentpay.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Lopez <maya.lopez@crescentpay.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spend compression & ops constraints — post-call recap and next steps

Irene — thanks, this is super helpful and captures it. Two clarifications from our side:

1) Budget: the $18k/month is the maximum the finance team will sign off on for any unvetted vendor for the first 30–60 day pilot; we can stretch to $22k only if we get clear SLA language and a predictable cap.

2) Token profile: we can export logs but we have PII in some request fields. We can deliver a token-only CSV (hashed ids + input/output token counts + route tag). I’ll ask engineering to prepare it — earliest we can get that is Mon 6/1 EOD.

Questions for your estimate:
- Can you give a quick delta on expected latency hit for the quantized path vs float baseline (ballpark 95p ms)?
- For batching window tuning: if we tighten to <10ms for auth flows, do you expect batching savings to materially drop?

Appreciate the quick turnaround. If you can get the two micro-profiles after Monday, that gives procurement something tangible for their review.

—Alex
Alex Dunn
Head of Platform Engineering | CrescentPay
alex.dunn@crescentpay.com | +1 (628) 555-0119


From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@crescentpay.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Lopez <maya.lopez@crescentpay.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spend compression & ops constraints — post-call recap and next steps

Alex / Maya — looping in a quick estimate and pilot suggestion per Irene’s note. Short answers to your questions above first:

- Quantized path latency: expect +8–18ms impact at 95p vs float baseline on comparable GPUs (depends on kernel fusion & sequence length). For short auth flows (avg 320 tokens) we typically observe 95p around 180–240ms depending on routing; quantization tends to add on the lower end of that range for tuned kernels.
- Batching <10ms: yes, with a sub-10ms window you get less batching headroom. For auth flows we recommend aggressive micro-batching with a 8–12ms window during off-peak and a <8ms fallback during peak for strict SLA adherence — that strategy usually preserves ~8–12% of batching savings vs the 12–20% conservative number.

Attached is a compact estimator (screenshot and the model sheet) and a short proposed pilot scope: 4 weeks, US-only, up to 150k requests, two model variants (quantized candidate + baseline), hourly usage reporting and one dashboard share. We’ll tune the router to prefer lower-latency hosts during peak.

Pilot quick numbers (conservative -> optimistic)
- Conserv: $18.5k/mo -> assumes 50% aggregate savings from batching + cache + q4bit, 95p ~235ms
- Opt: $12.8k/mo -> assumes 65% savings, 95p ~200ms

If procurement needs an additional comfort, Ben (cc’d) can outline an SLA carveout for the pilot window with credits for sustained latency regressions.

Attachments: crescentpay_pilot_scope.docx, crescentpay_token_profile_sample.csv (schema)

Happy to hop on a short call Mon if the token sample will be ready then.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Solution Economics Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@crescentpay.com>, Maya Lopez <maya.lopez@crescentpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spend compression & ops constraints — post-call recap and next steps

Perfect — thanks for the quick replies and the constraints clarity. Final items before we craft the pilot quote:

- Alex: if you can share the anonymized token CSV on Mon (6/1) we’ll run the two micro-profiles and return a per-token cost + 95p latency comparison by Tue 6/2 EOD.
- Ben: can you draft a short pilot SLA note (credits & latency carveouts) and a one-page procurement summary (numbers only) that I can forward to Alex? If you can drop those by Mon 9am PST that would be great.
- Alex / Maya: propose a 30-min kickoff Wed 6/3 10:00am PT to align on S3 access, pilot routing rules, and success criteria. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

I’ll also attach a compact quote and a one-page ROI brief after we run the micro-profiles. Thanks again — looking forward to moving this to a short pilot.

Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
